title: Integral strict-local sections agree with geometric-fibre sections
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, f:X→Y integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], s:Spec Ω→Y a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and (g′,f′,f,s) Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let F be a sheaf of Λ-modules on X_et [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use the adopted strict localization S_(s)=Spec(strictHenselization s) with its canonical structural map strictLocalizationToBase s [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit; def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Put Z=X×_Y S_(s), with projection p:Z→X. There exists a module isomorphism e:Γ(Z,p^*F)≅Γ(X′,g′^*F), evaluated on the identity etale object on X′. For every small-model affine pointed neighbourhood j=(V_j,v_j), qcqsStrictLocalSectionRestriction Λ f s F j followed by e.hom equals geometricFibreSectionRestriction Λ sq.toCommSq F V_j v_j [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-strict-local-module-comparison]. This compares sections on two schemes and asserts no neighbourhood representative existence. This is the full-model presentation of the former small-colimit statement under the canonical colimit and structural-map comparison.

proof.text: Use the existing adopted proof, without changing its Lean text. The full strictHenselization has the local-ring and henselian instances from Sites.StrictHenselizationLocal and separably closed residue field. Equip Ω with the algebra from descResidueField. The full-model strictHenselizationPointedMap constructs ψ and its pointed leg equations. Define t by Spec.map of ψ followed by the separable-closure inclusion. Cofilteredness gives one representative; its pointed equation and strictHenselizationStructuralMap_eq imply t followed by strictLocalizationToBase is s. These are the adopted full-model versions of the local-structure and pointed-map facts, canonically identified with the small model by smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso.

The adopted singleton-fibre theorem strictHenselizationStructuralMap_fiber_eq_closedPoint applied to t and the preceding equation identifies the image of the closed point with the closed point of the full strict henselization.

Construct i by pullback.lift from g′ and f′ followed by t. Its two projection equations and pullback pasting identify the closed geometric fibre square. Integrality survives base change. Apply isIso_integralStrictHenselianGeometricFibreRestriction to obtain invertibility of globalSectionsUpperStarMap along i.

Unfold the adopted concrete strictLocalFibreRestriction: its factors are the preceding global-section map, the inverse-image composition comparison and terminal evaluation, hence all are invertible. Take asIso of this restriction. Its representative equation is exactly the adopted strictLocalFibreRestriction_compatibility, applied to t, its pointed equations, i and its two projection equations. The adopted consumer already uses this full-model formula, so the old small-model theorem and its direct graph calculation are unnecessary.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_integralStrictLocalFibreComparison
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {X' X Y : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of Ω)} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f s) [IsIntegralHom f]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) :
    ∃ e : (Sheaf.Γ (pullback f (strictLocalizationToBase s)).smallEtaleTopology
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj
        ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)
          (pullback.fst f (strictLocalizationToBase s))).obj F) ≅
      ((g')^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ].obj F).obj.obj
        (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X'))),
      ∀ j : SmallModel.{u} (strictHenselizationNeighbourhoods s),
        qcqsStrictLocalSectionRestriction Λ f s F j ≫ e.hom =
          geometricFibreSectionRestriction Λ sq.toCommSq F
            ((AffineEtale.Spec Y).obj
              ((equivSmallModel.{u} (strictHenselizationNeighbourhoods s)).inverse.obj j).1)
            ((equivSmallModel.{u} (strictHenselizationNeighbourhoods s)).inverse.obj j).2

old_proof.text: Obtain the strict henselization local structure. Equip the geometric field with its residue-field algebra via descResidueField. The pointed-map theorem supplies the compatible ring map; construct t by Spec.map. Its pointed leg identity and the structural-map equation imply t followed by the structural map is s. Apply strictHenselizationStructuralMap_fiber_eq_closedPoint_compat from the canonical small-to-full comparison to this equation at the closed point; it puts the image of t at the closed point of the small model.

Construct i by pullback.lift from g′ and f′ followed by t. Its two projection equations follow by pullback.lift_fst and pullback.lift_snd. Pullback pasting yields the closed geometric fibre square. Integrality survives base change, and the integral strictly-henselian fibre restriction theorem makes the global-section map along i invertible.

Construct the required morphism r locally as the global inverse-image section map along i followed by the inverse-image composition comparison and terminal evaluation. Each factor is invertible, so take asIso r. For every small-model limit leg l apply unitSectionRestriction_comp. The graph of i followed by l agrees with geometricFibreSectionLift: the first projection follows from hi′, the first small-model projection identity and hpoint j; the second from hi and the second projection identity. Pullback hom-ext identifies the graphs. Expand unitSectionRestriction and cancel the terminal evaluation isomorphisms to get the required representative equation. This preserves the original small-model statement without the retired specialized definition or theorem.

Expand each former small-model qcqs restriction as unitSectionRestriction along the same small limit leg; expand the former comparison predicate as its germ equations. etaleSectionGraph is definitionally the former terminal graph. This changes only the spelling of the unit/restriction formulas and preserves every scheme, hypothesis, and conclusion.
